TITLE: As Iran talks stall, Israel and US prepping to renew war as soon as next week – report
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-16

Israel and the United States are carrying out their most intense preparations yet to renew attacks on Iran, possibly as soon as next week, two Middle Eastern officials told The New York Times on Friday.

Options cited by US officials include:
- A more intense bombing campaign against military and infrastructure sites
- Conquering Iran's key oil export hub of Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf
- Putting commandos on the mainland to extract nuclear material buried under the rubble

Extracting highly enriched uranium would risk several casualties and require thousands of supporting forces to create a perimeter.

A senior Israeli official quoted by Channel 12: "The Americans understand that negotiations with Iran are going nowhere. We're preparing for days to weeks of fighting and waiting for Trump's final decision. We'll know more in 24 hours."

Iran's stockpile of about 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium — enough for about ten nuclear warheads — is thought to have been buried following US strikes on key Iranian nuclear facilities during the 12-day Israel-Iran war in June 2025.

On Friday, Trump said he would accept a 20-year suspension of Iran's uranium enrichment program if Tehran gave a "real" guarantee, in an apparent shift from his earlier demand of permanent halt.

Iraq's new oil minister Basim Mohammed said Saturday that his country exported 10 million barrels via the strait in April, down from about 93 million barrels monthly before the Iran war (about 90% of Iraq's government budget revenues previously).
